Asymptotic Variance of the RG Failure Rate

Source: R/04_rg.R
vcov_rg.Rd

Compute the pointwise asymptotic variance of the plug-in RG failure-rate estimator for an irreducible finite-state Markov chain with fixed initial distribution.

Usage

vcov_rg(x, time, up)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A single nonnegative integer giving the discrete time point. Values must be less than .Machine$integer.max; missing and infinite values are not allowed.

up

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric scalar containing the variance in the \(\sqrt{n}\) limit of the RG estimator. Divide by the number of observed transitions \(n\) to approximate the estimator variance. This is a pointwise variance, not a joint covariance across times.

Details

Corollary 2 of Sadek and Limnios (2002, pp. 1851–1852) applies the delta method to \(r(t)=-\log(1-\lambda(t))\), giving $$\sigma_r^2(t)=\frac{\sigma_\lambda^2(t)}{(1-\lambda(t))^2}.$$ This function reuses vcov_bmp() for \(\sigma_\lambda^2(t)\) and the normalized survival recursion for \(1-\lambda(t)=R(t)/R(t-1)\). The scaling is performed by two successive divisions, avoiding premature underflow from squaring a small survival probability.

At positive times, both preceding and current survival must be positive. An error is raised for infinite or undefined RG rates, where Corollary 2 does not provide a finite-rate delta-method limit. At time zero the variance is zero when \(R(0)>0\), because the initial distribution is fixed. Full operational sets also have variance zero. Very small survival ratios can produce an asymptotic variance exceeding the numeric range.

References

Sadek, A., and Limnios, N. (2002). Asymptotic properties for maximum likelihood estimators for reliability and failure rates of Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 31(10), 1837–1861. doi:10.1081/STA-120014916 .

See also

rgf(), vcov_bmp()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
rgf(x, time = 0:3, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.9162907 0.2231436 0.2231436 0.2231436
vcov_rg(x, time = 3L, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.4166667
